facts.text: I've been feeling weak all over.
I've been getting weaker over the last few months.
I've been losing weight without trying.

facts.item: weight loss: change in diet or exercise
facts.text: I haven't changed my diet or how much I exercise.

facts.item: change in how often I urinate
facts.text: I haven't noticed any change in how often I pee.
It doesn't hurt or burn when I pee.

facts.item: getting up at night to urinate
facts.text: I don't have to get up at night to pee.
I don't have high blood pressure.
I haven't had any significant surgery.
Kidney disease runs in my family.
I'm worried about my kidney function because of the kidney disease in my family.
I work as a school teacher.

leakage.reason: 'kidney' is a gold-diagnosis word; the fact is the source's family history of kidney disease, not the patient's diagnosis.
'kidney' is a gold-diagnosis word; the patient's own worry about her kidney function is in the source (History and Secondary_Symptoms) and does not state the diagnosis.

source_issues: Secondary_Symptoms holds a denial ('No urinary symptoms') and a concern ('Concern about kidney disease'), not symptoms.
The family history of kidney disease sits in Past_Medical_History and the History; merged into f014.
notes: 'Feeling weaker over the last few months' gives the weakness its own duration child; weight loss 'despite no changes in diet or exercise' gives a context child stated as a denial.
The motor-strength result keeps the source's clause that the patient reports feeling weak, because it is part of the examiner's answer.

Gold aliases: 'chronic kidney disease'/'CKD' and 'chronic renal insufficiency' are not listed. Under KDIGO and MeSH, kidney failure is the advanced end of CKD, so CKD is the broader term; partial or full credit for 'CKD' is left to the judge. 'End-stage renal disease' is not listed either: the values (creatinine 2.3 mg/dL) do not establish end-stage disease.
Validator warning on x013 ('looks like review commentary') is a false positive: the pattern 'OCR' matches inside 'hematocrit'. The result is plain lab values.
Gold aliases added in harmonisation (chronic kidney disease, CKD, chronic renal insufficiency): Same aliases as case 159 (chronic kidney failure).

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a 40-year-old woman who has presented with weakness and weight loss, and interpret her laboratory findings to make a diagnosis.
